cards.title: Finite double-slit support
cards.role: Defines the exact finite aperture over which every generated Fresnel integral is evaluated.

checks.reason: The transmission and the two explicit integration intervals are stated in the main paper and Supplement S2.
The two rect supports are centered at -d/2 and +d/2 with half-width a/2, giving exactly the two stated finite intervals.

cards.numerical_form: Use independent Gauss--Legendre nodes on each interval [s*d/2-a/2, s*d/2+a/2] and concatenate the weighted sums; never integrate over source-image data.

cards.title: Fresnel field and baseline TRY response
cards.role: Defines the independently evaluated complex field, its zero-aberration limit, and the Fig. 1(a) observable.

checks.reason: The phase convention, detector coordinate, and omission of only overall constant Fresnel prefactors are explicit in the paper and supplement.
Setting both dimensionless aberration coefficients to zero removes only the last two phase factors, and the measured response is the real nonnegative modulus square.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the complex exponential at all y samples and finite-slit quadrature nodes; multiply by the quadrature weights to obtain E0, then compute R0=real(E0*conj(E0)).

cards.title: Weighted moments and exact local intensity derivatives
cards.role: Connects the physical Fresnel field to the tilt and defocus response functions plotted in Fig. 1(b).

checks.reason: Both weighted moments and the signed intensity derivatives are explicitly stated and derived in Supplement S1.
Differentiating exp(i*theta*q) gives i*q; applying d|E|^2=2 Re(E* dE) and Re(i z)=-Im(z) yields the stated factor and minus sign.
For point slits x=+/-W, q_f=1 so M_f=E0 and g_f=-2 Im(|E0|^2)=0, while q_t remains differential.

cards.numerical_form: Reuse the baseline phase matrix and evaluate weighted sums for q_t and q_f. Compute g_t and g_f from the complex cross-products, without finite differencing the plotted curves.

cards.title: Noise weight and full source-resolved Fisher matrix
cards.role: Defines the information benchmark used by Fig. 1(d) and Fig. S1.

checks.reason: The 2% regularizing floor and both full-Fisher representations are stated in the main text and Supplement S3.
Substituting s_mu=g_mu/N into <s_mu,s_nu>_N=integral N*s_mu*s_nu gives integral g_mu*g_nu/N exactly.
Because B is strictly positive and R0 is nonnegative, N is positive and the Fisher matrix is a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.

cards.numerical_form: Use the same trapezoidal y weights for every full/coded inner product. Assemble the symmetric 2x2 matrix from g_t, g_f, and positive N.

cards.title: Matched filters and nuisance-orthogonal source codes
cards.role: Defines the optimized code pair plotted in Fig. 1(c).
cards.latex: w_t^{\mathrm{raw}}=g_t/N,\quad w_f^{\mathrm{raw}}=g_f/N,\quad \widetilde w_t=w_t^{\mathrm{raw}}-\frac{\langle w_t^{\mathrm{raw}},1\rangle_N}{\langle1,1\rangle_N},\quad \widetilde w_f=w_f^{\mathrm{raw}}-\frac{\langle w_f^{\mathrm{raw}},1\rangle_N}{\langle1,1\rangle_N}-\frac{\langle w_f^{\mathrm{raw}},\widetilde w_t\rangle_N}{\langle\widetilde w_t,\widetilde w_t\rangle_N}\widetilde w_t,\quad w_\mu=\widetilde w_\mu/\|\widetilde w_\mu\|_N.

checks.reason: The raw weights, projection order, normalization, and discrete inner product are fully specified in Supplement S2.
Cauchy--Schwarz in the N metric maximizes the one-parameter SNR for w proportional to g/N.
Standard Gram--Schmidt algebra makes both codes orthogonal to the constant mode, mutually orthogonal, and unit norm in the N metric.

cards.numerical_form: Compute weighted projections with the common y integration weights; normalize only after subtracting the nuisance and preceding-code components. Record residual inner products as checks.

cards.title: Coded Fisher matrix and basis-independent retention
cards.role: Defines the optimized and toy principal information fractions plotted in Fig. 1(d).

checks.reason: The transfer, covariance, Fisher, projection interpretation, and retention matrix are all explicit in Supplement S3.
Under any nonsingular code-basis transform A, G->AG and Sigma->A Sigma A^T, so G^T Sigma^-1 G is unchanged.
Projection cannot add score-space information, so exact-arithmetic retention eigenvalues must lie in [0,1], up to numerical roundoff.

cards.numerical_form: Assemble G and Sigma with common y weights, solve linear systems rather than explicitly inverting Sigma, whiten F_code with the symmetric eigendecomposition of F_full, and sort retention eigenvalues ascending.

cards.title: Gaussian toy-code basis
cards.role: Defines the fair parity-only comparator in Fig. 1(c,d), using the same physical response and noise metric.
cards.latex: \bar y=\frac{\int yR_0dy}{\int R_0dy},\quad \sigma_y^2=\frac{\int(y-\bar y)^2R_0dy}{\int R_0dy},\quad \xi=(y-\bar y)/\sigma_y,\quad h_t^{(0)}=\xi,\quad h_f^{(0)}=(\xi^2-1)/\sqrt2,

checks.reason: Supplement S4 fully specifies the R0-derived coordinate, raw toy functions, and identical nuisance-orthogonal processing.
Applying the same constant removal, noise metric, orthogonalization, and normalization isolates the subspace choice as the only optimized-versus-toy difference.

cards.numerical_form: Compute ybar and sigma from independently generated R0, build the two raw templates, pass them through the same noise-metric Gram--Schmidt helper, and evaluate their Fisher retention with EQC006.

cards.title: Finite-width defocus visibility and width-scan ratio
cards.role: Defines the Fig. S1 quantity and its analytically verified narrow-slit limit.

source_refs.value: supplement.tex Eqs. (S71)-(S84), Table S1, and Fig. S1

checks.reason: The within-slit expansion, repeated-Fisher procedure, five widths, and exact ratio table are stated in Supplement S5.
At a->0 the non-common terms 2s*u/W and (u/W)^2 vanish, so the normalized quadratic phase becomes common mode and rho tends to zero.
Both theta parameters are dimensionless, so F_ff/F_tt is dimensionless and can be compared across slit widths.

cards.numerical_form: For every paper width in [20,40,80,150,250] micrometres, rebuild the finite-slit quadrature, E0, scores, N, and F_full; write rho=F_ff/F_tt without using Table S1 as an input.
